TOWER-v3 PARAGRAPH:
The five extra first-order flex directions of the d=6 Galois core are NOT
obstructed at second order.  The constraint map (norms and orthogonalities) is
exactly quadratic, so a first-order flex u extends to second order precisely
when its obstruction class [Q(u)] = [(1/2) D^2G(u,u)] vanishes in coker(J);
since Q is quadratic rather than linear the unobstructed set is a cone, and we
determine it completely rather than by sampling.  The class map is fixed by the
21 classes [B(u_i,u_j)] on a basis u_1,...,u_6 of ker(J)/gauge -- it descends to
that quotient because B(u,g) = -J.(L u) lies in range(J) for every gauge
generator g = L x0 -- and all 21 lie in range(J) exactly: flint solve on the
3039x3039 pivot subsystem, then J.h = Q verified on all 6848 rows in integer
arithmetic, independently at x5 = (3+4i)/5 and x13 = (5+12i)/13.  The quadratic
obstruction map ker(J)/gauge -> coker(J) is therefore identically zero: every
direction of the 6-dimensional flex space -- the mechanism direction v_theta,
each of the five extras, and every combination of them -- integrates to second
order.  The d=6 rung's excess flex is thus not killed by the leading
obstruction, and its departure from the flex = 1 pattern of d = 8, 10, 12
survives past first order.  The test is calibrated against the known-integrable
direction v_theta (which passes) and against two negative controls -- the same
quadratic term re-blocked in Kernaghan's Re-then-Im order, and a random integer
vector -- both of which are correctly rejected at rank 3040, so the membership
test is neither vacuous nor mis-indexed.
Scope: this settles SECOND order.  Third order does bite, and it is where
the flex space finally splits: running the same decision procedure on the
cubic class [B(u,h)] -- well defined because h is unique modulo ker J and
B(u, ker J) consists exactly of the 21 second-order classes just shown to
vanish -- gives 24 of the 56 symmetrised cubic coefficients NONZERO, at both
x5 and x13.  All six pure directions still survive (as v_theta must, its
circle being exact), and so does every element of the 3-dimensional
<v_theta, w3241, w3243> and of the 4-dimensional <v_theta, w3277, w3291,
w3301>; but every cross combination of the two groups, and every generic
direction of the 6-dimensional space, is obstructed at third order.  To
third order the deformation germ therefore looks like a union of two
branches through the Galois point rather than one smooth 6-parameter
family, and the honest statement for the tower is that the d=6 excess flex
is unobstructed at second order and only partially so at third.
